greek: Ὁ δὲ ὄφις ἦν φρονιμώτατος πάντων τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὧν ἐποίησεν κύριος ὁ θεός· καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ὄφις τῇ γυναικί Τί ὅτι εἶπεν ὁ θεός Οὐ μὴ φάγητε ἀπὸ παντὸς ξύλου τοῦ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ;
hint: The adjective for the serpent is the one Jesus tells his disciples to be.

notes.text: Middle Liddell gives one sense, *a serpent, snake*. The noun carries no judgement of its own; what the serpent is, the verse says with an adjective.

Superlative of φρόνιμος, whose first sense is *in one's right mind, in one's senses*; *staid, discreet* is its second and *wise, sensible, prudent* its third. It is not a word for cunning, and it is the adjective of Matthew 10:16: γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις. [[flag]] Hebrew *ʿārûm*, *shrewd, crafty*, puns on *ʿărûmmîm*, *naked*, in 2:25. Greek γυμνοί and φρόνιμος share nothing, and the pun is gone.

notes.lemma: τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
notes.text: *The wild animals upon the earth.* [[flag]] The Hebrew has *ḥayyat haśśādeh*, *the living things of the field*. The Greek widens the field to the earth, and does so again at 3:14.
The chapter's first κύριος: the title the Greek sets in place of the Hebrew divine name, as at 2:8.

τί in the accusative with ὅτι, *why is it that* — the construction of Luke 2:49, Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με. [[flag]] The Hebrew *ʾap kî-ʾāmar ʾĕlōhîm* is an exclamation as much as a question, *Indeed, has God said…*; the Greek asks for God's reason.

οὐ μή with the aorist subjunctive, the strongest denial Greek has: *by no means may you eat*. At 2:16 every tree but one was given; the serpent's version forbids them all, and the construction makes the overstatement emphatic.
Capitalised because each opens direct speech — the serpent's question, and the words it puts in God's mouth, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the serpent|the serpent, the snake|ὄφις]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[most in one's right mind|most in one's right mind, most in one's senses, most staid and unmoved and discreet, wisest, most sensible, most prudent|φρόνιμος]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the wild animals|of the wild animals, of the beasts, of the savage beasts, of the game|θηρίον]] of the things [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]], which [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]]; and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the serpent|the serpent, the snake|ὄφις]] [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman|γυνή]] why [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] no, [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may eat|you may eat, you may eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of wood|of wood, of timber, of a piece of wood|ξύλον]] of the thing [[in the park|within, inside of, and by means of the park, the garden of Eden, paradise|ἐν; παράδεισος]]?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ἡ γυνὴ τῷ ὄφει Ἀπὸ καρποῦ ξύλου τοῦ παραδείσου φαγόμεθα,
hint: The woman answers the serpent's 'no tree' with the permission as it was given.

notes.text: Future of ἐσθίω, *we will eat*, as φάγῃ was future at 2:16. The sentence does not end here: Rahlfs prints a comma, and the prohibition follows in 3:3.
καρπός is *fruit* first, then *produce, returns, profits*, then *result*. The tree has not been said to bear fruit before this verse; 2:16 gave *every tree*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] [[to the serpent|to the serpent, to the snake|ὄφις]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of fruit|of fruit, of produce, of returns, of profits, of result|καρπός]] [[of wood|of wood, of timber, of a piece of wood|ξύλον]] [[of the park|of the park, of the garden of Eden, of paradise|παράδεισος]] [[we will eat|we will eat, we will eat of|ἐσθίω]],

greek: ἀπὸ δὲ καρποῦ τοῦ ξύλου, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ παραδείσου, εἶπεν ὁ θεός Οὐ φάγεσθε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ μὴ ἅψησθε αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνητε.
hint: The woman adds a prohibition the command in 2:17 does not contain.

notes.text: *Nor may you touch it.* The command as 2:16–17 gives it, in Greek and in Hebrew alike, says nothing of touching. The woman's report adds it.

Middle of ἅπτω. The entry's first sense, *to fasten, bind fast*, is the active; its second is marked *Mid.* and takes the genitive, as here — *to fasten oneself to, cling to, hang on by, lay hold of, grasp, touch*. The headword takes that sense, the form's own.
Masculine. The pronoun takes up the fronted ἀπὸ καρποῦ, repeating its preposition, not the neuter ξύλον beside it: it is the fruit that may not be eaten or touched.

notes.lemma: ὅ ἐστιν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ παραδείσου
notes.text: At 2:9 it was the tree of life that stood ἐν μέσῳ; the woman places the forbidden tree there. Revelation 2:7 describes the tree of life with nearly the same clause: ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

An adverb of place in the lexicon's first sense, *there, where*, and a conjunction in its second, *that, in order that*. Used as a conjunction, it takes the first conjunction sense, as a word used as a noun takes the first noun sense.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech — the command as the woman repeats it, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of fruit|of fruit, of produce, of returns, of profits, of result|καρπός]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]], which is [[in middle|within, inside of, and by means of the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἐν; μέσος]] [[of the park|of the park, of the garden of Eden, of paradise|παράδεισος]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] not [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] it [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all|οὐδέ]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may fasten yourselves to|you may fasten yourselves to, you may cling to, you may hang on by, you may lay hold of, you may grasp, you may touch|ἅπτω]] it, [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may die off|you may die off, you may die, you may be put to death, you may be slain|ἀποθνήσκω]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ὄφις τῇ γυναικί Οὐ θανάτῳ ἀποθανεῖσθε·
hint: God's sentence from 2:17, word for word, with one word put in front of it.

notes.text: The sentence of 2:17, θανάτῳ ἀποθανεῖσθε, with οὐ set before it. The serpent does not argue with the command; it negates it, in its own words.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the serpent|the serpent, the snake|ὄφις]] [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman|γυνή]] not [[to death|to death, to the death threatened, to the sentence of death|θάνατος]] [[you will die off|you will die off, you will die, you will be put to death, you will be slain|ἀποθνήσκω]];

greek: ᾔδει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἐν ᾗ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγητε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, διανοιχθήσονται ὑμῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί, καὶ ἔσεσθε ὡς θεοὶ γινώσκοντες καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν.
hint: The Hebrew can be read 'like God' or 'like gods'; the Greek has to choose.

notes.text: Pluperfect of οἶδα, whose perfect is a present, *I know*; its pluperfect is a past, *knew*. [[flag]] The Hebrew *yōdēaʿ* is a participle, *God knows*. The Greek puts the knowing in the past.

notes.lemma: ἐν ᾗ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγητε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ
notes.text: God's words from 2:17, ᾗ δʼ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγητε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, taken up with ἐν added — and given another ending.
Plural: *as gods*. [[flag]] Hebrew *kēʾlōhîm* can be read *like God* or *like gods*, since *ʾĕlōhîm* is plural in form either way. The Greek must decide, and decides for the plural.
One Middle Liddell entry holds two words: ὥς, accented, the demonstrative *so, thus*, and ὡς, the relative *as*. Rahlfs prints the relative, and its glosses are the chain.
γινώσκω, not οἶδα: the verb of the tree's name at 2:17, knowledge come by. Present participle — knowing as a lasting condition.
Used as a noun, and so takes καλός's first noun sense, *beauty*, as at 2:9; πονηρόν keeps the adjective's senses, the entry giving its neuter none.

reading: [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[knew|knew, was assured, was versed in|οἶδα]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to which ever [[to day|to day, to day-break, to time|ἡμέρα]] [[you may eat|you may eat, you may eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] it, [[will be opened|will be opened, will be opened and explained|διανοίγω]] of you [[the eyes|the eyes, the dearest and best, the comfort, the buds|ὀφθαλμός]], and you will be [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[gods|gods, the gods, goddesses|θεός]] [[learning to know|learning to know, perceiving, marking, learning, discerning and distinguishing|γινώσκω]] [[beauty|beauty, moral beauty and virtue|καλός]] and [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked|πονηρός]].

greek: καὶ εἶδεν ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι καλὸν τὸ ξύλον εἰς βρῶσιν καὶ ὅτι ἀρεστὸν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἰδεῖν καὶ ὡραῖόν ἐστιν τοῦ κατανοῆσαι, καὶ λαβοῦσα τοῦ καρποῦ αὐτοῦ ἔφαγεν· καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς μετʼ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔφαγον.
hint: The Hebrew says he ate; the Greek says they ate.

notes.text: Three things seen: *beautiful* for eating, *acceptable* to the eyes to look at, and *produced at the right season* to observe. κατανοέω is *to observe well, to understand* — to take something in with the mind. [[flag]] The Hebrew has *a delight to the eyes* and *desirable to make one wise*, *lĕhaśkîl*. The Greek keeps the looking and loses the wanting: nothing in the sentence desires wisdom.
Third plural, *they ate*. [[flag]] The Hebrew *wayyōʾkal* is singular, *and he ate*. The Greek has the man and the woman eat together.
καί here is *also*: she gave also to her man. ἀνήρ, the male, as at 2:23 — not ἄνθρωπος.
μετά with the genitive opens at *in the midst of, among*; *along with* is its second sense and *with* its third. The Hebrew has the same, *ʿimmāh*, *with her*.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[beautiful|beautiful, beauteous, fair, good|καλός]] [[the wood|the wood, the timber, the piece of wood|ξύλον]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[meat|meat, eating, corrosion and rust|βρῶσις]] and [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[acceptable|acceptable, pleasing|ἀρεστός]] [[to the eyes|to the eyes, to the dearest and best, to the comfort, to the buds|ὀφθαλμός]] [[to see|to see, to perceive, to behold, to look at|ὁράω]] and [[produced at the right season|produced at the right season, seasonable, timely, happening in season and done in due season, due and proper, ripe, in the bloom of youth and blooming, beautiful|ὡραῖος]] is [[of the observing well|of the observing well, of the understanding, of the perceiving, of the learning, of the considering|κατανοέω]], and [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[of the fruit|of the fruit, of the produce, of the returns and profits, of the result|καρπός]] of it [[ate|ate, ate of|ἐσθίω]]; and [[gave|gave, granted, provided, gave over and delivered up|δίδωμι]] [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] [[to the man|to the man, to the man in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] of her [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] her, and [[they ate|they ate, they ate of|ἐσθίω]].

greek: καὶ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ τῶν δύο, καὶ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι γυμνοὶ ἦσαν, καὶ ἔρραψαν φύλλα συκῆς καὶ ἐποίησαν ἑαυτοῖς περιζώματα.
hint: The eyes are opened, as the serpent promised, and what they see is that they are naked.

notes.text: The serpent's verb from 3:5, διανοιχθήσονται, now in the aorist: the promise is kept in the words it was made in. διανοίγω is *to open*; its second sense, *to open and explain*, is the New Testament's — Luke 24:32, ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς.
γινώσκω, the verb of the tree at 2:17 and of the promise at 3:5. What they come to know is that they are naked.
The word of 2:25, where it stood beside *not ashamed*, and the same imperfect, ἦσαν. γυμνός runs on to *unarmed, uncovered*.
*A girdle round the loins, apron* — a band, not a garment. Hebrew *ḥăgōrōt*, belts, is the same.

reading: and [[were opened|were opened, were opened and explained|διανοίγω]] [[the eyes|the eyes, the dearest and best, the comfort, the buds|ὀφθαλμός]] of the two, and [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished|γινώσκω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[naked|naked, unclad, unarmed, uncovered, stripped of|γυμνός]] they were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, and [[sewed|sewed, stitched together, devised and contrived and plotted|ῥάπτω]] [[leaves|leaves, foliage, petals, herbs|φύλλον]] [[of fig-tree|of fig-tree, of fig|συκῆ]] and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] for themselves [[girdles round the loins|girdles round the loins, aprons|περίζωμα]].

greek: Καὶ ἤκουσαν τὴν φωνὴν κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ περιπατοῦντος ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τὸ δειλινόν, καὶ ἐκρύβησαν ὅ τε Αδαμ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ ξύλου τοῦ παραδείσου.
hint: The Hebrew has the wind of the day; the Greek has the evening.

notes.text: Accusative of time, *at evening*. Middle Liddell files δειλινός as a contraction of δειελινός and gives that entry one sense, *at evening*, so there is no range to open and it stands as plain text. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lĕrûaḥ hayyôm*, *at the wind of the day* — *rûaḥ*, the word behind πνεῦμα at 1:2. The Greek gives the hour and drops the wind.

φωνή's first sense is *a sound, tone*; *the voice* follows it. The participle is genitive masculine, so it goes with κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ, not with φωνήν: the sound of the lord God, walking. Hebrew *qôl* is likewise both sound and voice.
Aorist passive of κρύπτω, *were hidden*. The entry gives the passive its own gloss, *to hide oneself, lie hidden*, and the chain carries both.
*From face* — πρόσωπον again, and here the Greek keeps the Hebrew's *face*, *mippĕnê*, as it did at 2:6.
First occurrence in this chapter, so glossed again.

reading: And [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[the sound|the sound, the tone, the sound of the voice, the cry, the faculty of speech and discourse, the language, the saying|φωνή]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only|θεός]] [[of walking up and down|of walking up and down, of walking about, of walking, of living|περιπατέω]] [[in the park|within, inside of, and by means of the park, the garden of Eden, paradise|ἐν; παράδεισος]] at evening, and [[were hidden|were hidden, were covered and cloaked, hid themselves and lay hidden, were concealed and kept secret|κρύπτω]] [[and|and, both and, and also|τε]] the [[name:Αδαμ]] and [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of him [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of face|of face, of visage, of countenance, of look, of outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only|θεός]] [[in middle|within, inside of, and by means of the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἐν; μέσος]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]] [[of the park|of the park, of the garden of Eden, of paradise|παράδεισος]].

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν Αδαμ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Αδαμ, ποῦ εἶ;
hint: The Hebrew question is one word; the Greek puts the man's name in front of it.

notes.text: *Adam, where are you?* [[flag]] The Hebrew is one word, *ʾayyekkâ*, *where are you?*, with no name. The Greek adds the vocative.
*Where?* first; *how? by what right?* in the entry's second sense.
Twice here, both bare: glossed at 3:8.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] the [[name:Αδαμ]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[name:Αδαμ]], [[where|where, at what point, how, by what right|ποῦ]] are you?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τὴν φωνήν σου ἤκουσα περιπατοῦντος ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ καὶ ἐφοβήθην, ὅτι γυμνός εἰμι, καὶ ἐκρύβην.
hint: Afraid — and the lexicon's first sense for the verb is to be put to flight.

notes.text: Aorist passive of φοβέομαι, which Middle Liddell files under φοβέω. The entry's actives — *to put to flight, to terrify* — are skipped by name; its passive opens *to be put to flight, to flee affrighted*, and only after that *to be seized with fear, fear*. In the lexicon's order, fear is a running away before it is a feeling.
Genitive, with σου: *your sound, walking*. [[flag]] The Hebrew has *I heard the sound of you in the garden*; the Greek adds *walking*, from 3:8.
Present: *I am naked*. The next verse asks how he knows it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[the sound|the sound, the tone, the sound of the voice, the cry, the faculty of speech and discourse, the language, the saying|φωνή]] of you [[I heard|I heard, I had hearing of, I heard tell of, I hearkened and gave ear, I listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[of walking up and down|of walking up and down, of walking about, of walking, of living|περιπατέω]] [[in the park|within, inside of, and by means of the park, the garden of Eden, paradise|ἐν; παράδεισος]] and [[I was put to flight|I was put to flight, I fled affrighted, I fled, I was seized with fear, I was affrighted, I feared|φοβέομαι]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[naked|naked, unclad, unarmed, uncovered, stripped of|γυμνός]] I am, and [[I was hidden|I was hidden, I was covered and cloaked, I hid myself and lay hidden, I was concealed|κρύπτω]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τίς ἀνήγγειλέν σοι ὅτι γυμνὸς εἶ; μὴ ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου, οὗ ἐνετειλάμην σοι τούτου μόνου μὴ φαγεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ἔφαγες;
hint: Two questions, and the punctuation between them is Rahlfs's own.

notes.text: Rahlfs's punctuation, which his apparatus marks as his: a question, then a second one opened by μή, which expects *no* — *you did not eat from the tree…, did you?* [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads εἶ, εἰ μή: *who told you that you are naked, unless you ate from the tree…* — one question, with its answer inside it.
*Of this one alone.* [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, which has *which I commanded you not to eat from*. The Greek narrows the command to the single tree, in God's own words, and does so again at 3:17.
ἀναγγέλλω, *to carry back tidings of, report* — news brought back from somewhere.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him who [[carried back tidings of|carried back tidings of, reported|ἀναγγέλλω]] to you [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[naked|naked, unclad, unarmed, uncovered, stripped of|γυμνός]] you are? [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]], of which [[I enjoined|I enjoined, I commanded|ἐντέλλομαι]] to you [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] [[of alone|of alone, of left alone, of forsaken and solitary, of only|μόνος]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[to eat|to eat, to eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] it, [[you ate|you ate, you ate of|ἐσθίω]]?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Αδαμ Ἡ γυνή, ἣν ἔδωκας μετʼ ἐμοῦ, αὕτη μοι ἔδωκεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου, καὶ ἔφαγον.
hint: Asked about the tree, the man answers about the woman.

notes.lemma: Ἡ γυνή, ἣν ἔδωκας μετʼ ἐμοῦ
notes.text: The answer opens with the woman and with God's giving of her: *the woman whom you gave with me*. μετά with the genitive, as the Hebrew *ʿimmādî*.
αὕτη, *this one*, stands first: she, and no other, gave.
First singular here, *I ate*, where the same form was third plural at 3:6.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῇ γυναικί Τί τοῦτο ἐποίησας; καὶ εἶπεν ἡ γυνή Ὁ ὄφις ἠπάτησέν με, καὶ ἔφαγον.
hint: The verb is the one Paul uses of this moment, with a prefix added.

notes.text: ἀπατάω, *to cheat, trick, outwit, beguile*. 2 Corinthians 11:3 uses the compound of this moment, ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐξηπάτησεν Εὕαν, and 1 Timothy 2:14 has both verbs: Ἀδὰμ οὐκ ἠπατήθη, ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἐξαπατηθεῖσα.
τί as at 3:1, *why*, with τοῦτο the object: *why did you do this?* The Hebrew *mah-zōʾt ʿāśît* is *what is this you have done?*
Capitalised because each opens direct speech — God's question, and the woman's answer, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman|γυνή]] why [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[you made|you made, you did, you produced, you created|ποιέω]]? and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] [[the serpent|the serpent, the snake|ὄφις]] [[cheated|cheated, tricked, outwitted, beguiled, deceived|ἀπατάω]] me, and [[I ate|I ate, I ate of|ἐσθίω]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ ὄφει Ὅτι ἐποίησας τοῦτο, ἐπικατάρατος σὺ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς· ἐπὶ τῷ στήθει σου καὶ τῇ κοιλίᾳ πορεύσῃ καὶ γῆν φάγῃ πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς σου.
hint: Cursed beyond every animal, and the Greek adds the breast to the belly.

notes.text: Middle Liddell gives one sense, *yet more accursed* — ἐπί added to κατάρατος, *accursed* — so there is no range to open and it stands as plain text. ἀπὸ πάντων is comparative, after the Hebrew *min*: accursed beyond all the flocks and the wild animals. Galatians 3:13 quotes the word from Deuteronomy: Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου.
[[flag]] *Of the earth*, where the Hebrew has *of the field*, as at 3:1.

notes.lemma: ἐπὶ τῷ στήθει σου καὶ τῇ κοιλίᾳ
notes.text: κοιλία's first sense is *the large cavity of the body*; *the belly* follows. [[flag]] The Hebrew has only *ʿal-gĕḥōnĕkā*, *upon your belly*. The Greek adds the breast.
*You will eat earth.* [[flag]] Hebrew *ʿāpār*, *dust*, which the Greek rendered χοῦν at 2:7 and renders γῆ here and at 3:19.
Future of πορεύομαι, the verb of the Tigris at 2:14: *being driven, carried, going*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[to the serpent|to the serpent, to the snake|ὄφις]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[you made|you made, you did, you produced, you created|ποιέω]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]], yet more accursed you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the flocks and herds|of the flocks and herds, of the single beasts, of the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the wild animals|of the wild animals, of the beasts, of the savage beasts, of the game|θηρίον]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]]; [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to the breast|to the breast, to the breast as the seat of feeling, to the heart|στῆθος]] of you and [[to the large cavity of the body|to the large cavity of the body, to the belly, to the intestines, to the bowels|κοιλία]] [[you will be driven|you will be driven, you will be carried, you will go, you will walk, you will march, you will go across and pass|πορεύομαι]] and [[earth|earth, land, ground|γῆ]] [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times|ἡμέρα]] [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]] of you.

greek: καὶ ἔχθραν θήσω ἀνὰ μέσον σου καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματός σου καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς· αὐτός σου τηρήσει κεφαλήν, καὶ σὺ τηρήσεις αὐτοῦ πτέρναν.
hint: The pronoun is masculine; the noun it follows is neuter.

notes.text: Masculine, where σπέρμα before it is neuter; a pronoun agreeing with it would be αὐτό. The Hebrew *hûʾ* is masculine and agrees with *zeraʿ*, which is masculine in Hebrew. Read as agreeing by sense with a collective *seed*, the Greek means the offspring; read as a single male descendant, it means one person. The grammar permits both and does not choose between them.

τηρέω, *to watch over, protect, guard*, then *to watch narrowly*, *to watch for* — the same verb both times. [[flag]] The Hebrew uses *šûp* twice, a verb whose sense is disputed: *bruise, crush*, or *snap at*. The Greek has a verb of watching, not of striking.
ἀνά with the accusative, *up to, up along*, with μέσον, *the middle*: together the idiom *between*. The reading gives the lexicon's parts and the idiom is recorded here, as κατὰ ἀνατολάς was at 2:8.
σπέρμα's first sense is *that which is sown* — the seed of plants — then *offspring, issue*, then *race, descent*.
Middle Liddell heads the entry with the Ionic spelling, ἔχθρη: *hatred, enmity*, *hostility*.

reading: and [[hatred|hatred, enmity, hatred for and enmity to, feud, hostility|ἔχθρα]] [[I will set|I will set, I will put, I will place, I will plant, I will lay|τίθημι]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of you and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of the woman|of the woman, of the mistress and lady, of the wife and spouse|γυνή]] and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of that which is sown|of that which is sown, of the seed, of the germ and origin and element, of the offspring and issue, of the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of that which is sown|of that which is sown, of the seed, of the germ and origin and element, of the offspring and issue, of the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of her; he of you [[will watch over|will watch over, will protect and guard, will give heed to and watch narrowly, will watch for, will keep|τηρέω]] [[head|head, the life, the top, the brim, the coping, the source, the crown and completion|κεφαλή]], and you [[will watch over|will watch over, will protect and guard, will give heed to and watch narrowly, will watch for, will keep|τηρέω]] of him [[heel|heel, the under part of the heel, the ham|πτέρνα]].

greek: καὶ τῇ γυναικὶ εἶπεν Πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὰς λύπας σου καὶ τὸν στεναγμόν σου, ἐν λύπαις τέξῃ τέκνα· καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἡ ἀποστροφή σου, καὶ αὐτός σου κυριεύσει.
hint: The Hebrew word is desire; the Greek word is a turning.

notes.text: ἀποστροφή is *a turning back*, then *a turning away from, an escape*, then *a resort, resource*. No verb: *toward your man, your turning*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *tĕšûqātēk*, *your desire*. The Greek word is the one that renders *tĕšûbātēk*, *your return* — a word one letter away.
*Your sighing, groaning, moaning.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *hērōnēk*, *your conception*, *your pregnancy*.
Participle and finite verb of one root, *multiplying I will multiply*: Greek imitating the Hebrew infinitive absolute, *harbâ ʾarbeh*, as βρώσει φάγῃ did at 2:16.
Verb and object from one root, τίκτω and τέκνον. The lexicon's first sense for τέκνον is *that which is borne*; *a child* comes with it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman|γυνή]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[making full|making full, increasing, multiplying|πληθύνω]] [[I will make full|I will make full, I will increase, I will multiply|πληθύνω]] [[the pains of body|the pains of body, the distresses and sad plights, the pains of mind, the griefs|λύπη]] of you and [[the sighing|the sighing, the groaning, the moaning|στεναγμός]] of you, [[in pains of body|within, inside of, and by means of pains of body, distresses and sad plights, pains of mind, griefs|ἐν; λύπη]] [[you will bring into the world|you will bring into the world, you will bring forth, you will bear, you will produce|τίκτω]] [[things borne|things borne, the born, children, the young|τέκνον]]; and [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the man|the man, the man in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] of you [[the turning back|the turning back, the turning away from, the escape from, the resort and resource|ἀποστροφή]] of you, and he of you [[will be lord|will be lord, will be master of, will have legal power|κυριεύω]].

greek: τῷ δὲ Αδαμ εἶπεν Ὅτι ἤκουσας τῆς φωνῆς τῆς γυναικός σου καὶ ἔφαγες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου, οὗ ἐνετειλάμην σοι τούτου μόνου μὴ φαγεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ἐπικατάρατος ἡ γῆ ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις σου· ἐν λύπαις φάγῃ αὐτὴν πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς σου·
hint: The earth is cursed, not the man — and 'because of you' has become 'in your works'.

notes.lemma: ἐπικατάρατος ἡ γῆ ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις σου
notes.text: The earth is accursed; the man is not. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *baʿăbûrekā*, *on account of you*. The Greek *in your works* is what *baʿăbōdekā* would give — the same letters but one, *d* for *r*, two letters easily confused in Hebrew script.
ἀκούω with the genitive: *to hearken, to listen to*, and in its fourth sense *to obey*. The same noun as at 3:8 and 3:10, where it was the sound of God walking.
[[flag]] *This one alone*, added again, as at 3:11.
Rahlfs ends the clause here, with Grabe's edition. Codex Alexandrinus adds ἔφαγες, *you ate*, as at the end of 3:11.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to the [[name:Αδαμ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[you heard|you heard, you had hearing of, you heard tell of, you hearkened and gave ear, you listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[of the sound|of the sound, of the tone, of the sound of the voice, of the cry, of the faculty of speech and discourse, of the language, of the saying|φωνή]] [[of the woman|of the woman, of the mistress and lady, of the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of you and [[you ate|you ate, you ate of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]], of which [[I enjoined|I enjoined, I commanded|ἐντέλλομαι]] to you [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] [[of alone|of alone, of left alone, of forsaken and solitary, of only|μόνος]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[to eat|to eat, to eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] it, yet more accursed [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[in the works|within, inside of, and by means of the works, the business, the deeds|ἐν; ἔργον]] of you; [[in pains of body|within, inside of, and by means of pains of body, distresses and sad plights, pains of mind, griefs|ἐν; λύπη]] [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of|ἐσθίω]] it [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times|ἡμέρα]] [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]] of you;

greek: ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀνατελεῖ σοι, καὶ φάγῃ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
hint: The second word is a spiked iron for laming horses before it is a weed.

notes.text: τρίβολος is first *a caltrop*, a three-spiked iron thrown down to lame an enemy's horses; *a prickly plant, a burr, thistle* is its second sense, marked New Testament. Hebrews 6:8 has the pair from this verse: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους.
ἀνατέλλω, the verb of 2:5, where nothing had yet risen up from the ground.
χόρτος and ἀγρός as at 2:5, where there was not yet any χόρτος ἀγροῦ. Now the man is to eat it.

reading: [[thorns|thorns, prickles, prickly plants, thistles, thistledown, spines|ἄκανθα]] and [[caltrops|caltrops, three-spiked implements, prickly plants, burrs, thistles, threshing-boards|τρίβολος]] [[will make to rise up|will make to rise up, will grow up, will give birth to and bring to light, will rise, will take its rise, will grow|ἀνατέλλω]] to you, and [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[the inclosed place|the inclosed place, the feeding-place, the feeding-ground, the food and fodder and provender, the grass, the hay|χόρτος]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country|ἀγρός]].

greek: ἐν ἱδρῶτι τοῦ προσώπου σου φάγῃ τὸν ἄρτον σου ἕως τοῦ ἀποστρέψαι σε εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐξ ἧς ἐλήμφθης· ὅτι γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ. —
hint: Dust in the Hebrew, earth in the Greek, and the verb for returning comes too early.

notes.lemma: γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿāpār ʾattâ wĕʾel-ʿāpār tāšûb*, *dust you are and to dust you will return*. The Greek has γῆ, *earth*, both times — not the χοῦς of 2:7 — and for *return* it has ἀπέρχομαι, *to go away, depart*. The verb of returning, ἀποστρέφω, stands earlier in the verse, for the Hebrew's first *šûb*.

ἕως with the articular infinitive, a construction Middle Liddell cites in the entry itself, ἕως τοῦ ἀποτῖσαι. ἀποστρέφω's first sense is transitive, *to turn*; here σε is its subject, and the use is the entry's intransitive, *to turn back*.
*Out of which you were taken* — the verb of the rib at 2:22–23, now of the man and the earth.
Rahlfs's paragraph dash, as after 2:20. It stands in the Greek line and not in the reading.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Αδαμ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτοῦ Ζωή, ὅτι αὕτη μήτηρ πάντων τῶν ζώντων.
hint: The Greek translates her name, and so keeps the pun the Hebrew makes on it.

notes.text: Hebrew *Ḥawwâ*, which the verse itself ties to *ḥay*, *living*. The Greek does not transliterate the name but translates it — Ζωή, *life* — and Rahlfs capitalises it as a name.
Translating the name keeps the verse's reason intact: Ζωή, because she is mother of all τῶν ζώντων. [[flag]] At 4:1 the Greek transliterates the same name, Ευαν, and the play is not made again.
No verb: *this one, mother of all the living*. The Hebrew has *hāyĕtâ*, *she was*.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Αδαμ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the woman|of the woman, of the mistress and lady, of the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of him [[name:Ζωή]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[mother|mother, dam, source|μήτηρ]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the living|of the living, of the alive, of those in full life and strength, of the fresh and strong|ζάω]].

greek: Καὶ ἐποίησεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ Αδαμ καὶ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ χιτῶνας δερματίνους καὶ ἐνέδυσεν αὐτούς. —
hint: Garments of skin, and the verb is one of clothing someone else.

notes.text: χιτών is *the garment worn next the skin, a frock* — the tunic, with a mantle over it — and δερμάτινος is *of skin, leathern*. The περιζώματα of 3:7 were girdles; these are garments.
ἐνδύω's first sense, *to go into, put on*, is dressing oneself; the entry marks the aorist ἐνέδυσα causal, *to clothe* another, and that is this form. They are clothed; they do not dress.
Rahlfs's paragraph dash again, in the Greek line and not in the reading.

reading: And [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to the [[name:Αδαμ]] and [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman|γυνή]] of him [[garments worn next the skin|garments worn next the skin, frocks, coats of mail, coverings, skins|χιτών]] [[of skin|of skin, leathern|δερμάτινος]] and [[clothed in|clothed in, clothed|ἐνδύω]] them.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός Ἰδοὺ Αδαμ γέγονεν ὡς εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν τοῦ γινώσκειν καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν, καὶ νῦν μήποτε ἐκτείνῃ τὴν χεῖρα καὶ λάβῃ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ φάγῃ καὶ ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
hint: Three verbs of what may happen, and a fourth of what will.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints ὁ θεός alone, with Codex Coislinianus (M). [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads κύριος ὁ θεός, and Origen's recension carries κύριος under the asterisk — his sign for words in the Hebrew that the Greek lacked. The Hebrew has *YHWH ʾĕlōhîm*.
[[flag]] Hebrew *hāʾādām*, with the article: *the man*. The Greek reads the name.
Perfect of γίνομαι: not *became* but *has come to be*, and stands so.
First person plural in God's mouth, as ποιήσωμεν at 2:18. The Greek renders it exactly and adds nothing to explain it.

Three subjunctives under μήποτε — *lest he stretch out, take, eat* — and then a future indicative, ζήσεται, *and he will live*: the last verb states an outcome, not a fear. Neither the Greek nor the Hebrew finishes the sentence; what God does follows in 3:23.

αἰών is first *a period of existence, one's life-time*, then *an age*, then *a long space of time*; the lexicon records εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας as *for ever*. The idiom is noted here and the reading prints the lexicon's range.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.
Used as a noun, and so takes καλός's first noun sense, *beauty*, as at 2:9; πονηρόν keeps the adjective's senses, the entry giving its neuter none.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[name:Αδαμ]] [[has come into being|has come to be and stands so, has arisen and remains arisen, has been brought into existence and continues so|γίνομαι]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[one|one, a single one, one alone|εἷς]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] us [[of the learning to know|of the learning to know, of the perceiving, of the marking, of the learning, of the discerning and distinguishing|γινώσκω]] [[beauty|beauty, moral beauty and virtue|καλός]] and [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked|πονηρός]], and [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]] [[that at no time|that at no time, lest ever, never, on no account, perhaps|μήποτε]] [[he may stretch out|he may stretch out, he may spread out, he may put forth|ἐκτείνω]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm|χείρ]] and [[he may take|he may take, he may receive, he may take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]] [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]] and [[he may eat|he may eat, he may eat of|ἐσθίω]] and [[he will live|he will live, he will be in full life and strength, he will be fresh and strong|ζάω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the period of existence|the period of existence, the life-time and life, the age and generation, the long space of time, the era and epoch, the world|αἰών]].

greek: καὶ ἐξαπέστειλεν αὐτὸν κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τοῦ παραδείσου τῆς τρυφῆς ἐργάζεσθαι τὴν γῆν, ἐξ ἧς ἐλήμφθη.
hint: This time the Greek translates Eden instead of transliterating it.

notes.text: *The park of softness, of luxury.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *gan-ʿēden*, *the garden of Eden*. At 2:8 and 2:10 the Greek transliterated the name, Εδεμ; here it translates it with τρυφή — *softness, delicacy, luxury* — the sense *ʿēden* has as a common noun.
ἐξαποστέλλω, a double compound, ἐκ and ἀπό with στέλλω: *to send quite away*.
The task of 2:5, where there was no man to work the earth, and of 2:15, where he was set in the park to work it. The same verb, now outside.

reading: and [[sent quite away|sent quite away, dispatched|ἐξαποστέλλω]] him [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the park|of the park, of the garden of Eden, of paradise|παράδεισος]] [[of the softness|of the softness, of the delicacy and daintiness, of the luxuries, of the luxuriousness and wantonness|τρυφή]] [[to work|to work, to labour, to work at and make and build, to do and perform and accomplish, to work the land, to earn by working|ἐργάζομαι]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] which [[was taken|was taken, was received, was taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]].

greek: καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὸν Αδαμ καὶ κατῴκισεν αὐτὸν ἀπέναντι τοῦ παραδείσου τῆς τρυφῆς καὶ ἔταξεν τὰ χερουβιμ καὶ τὴν φλογίνην ῥομφαίαν τὴν στρεφομένην φυλάσσειν τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς.
hint: The verb that set the man to guard the garden in 2:15 now guards it against him.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *wayyaškēn miqqedem lĕgan-ʿēden ʾet-hakkĕrubîm*, *and he stationed east of the garden of Eden the cherubim*. The Greek makes the man the object — he *settled him opposite* the park — and gives the cherubim a verb of their own, ἔταξεν.
κατοικίζω, *to remove to a place, and settle or establish there as colonists*: the verb of founding a colony.

Transliterated, and neuter here, τά. Rahlfs prints the Hebrew plural ending in -ιμ; Codex Alexandrinus has -ιν, as Hebrews 9:5 does, Χερουβὶν δόξης. τάσσω is *to arrange, put in order*, first of troops drawn up for battle.

Middle Liddell has no φλόγινος; LSJ gives *flaming, fiery* and cites this verse. ῥομφαία is *a large sword, scymitar*, a Thracian blade — the word of Luke 2:35 and of the sword from the mouth in Revelation 1:16. The participle is middle or passive, and the entry's passive and middle open *to turn oneself, to turn round*.

φυλάσσω, *to keep watch and ward*, the verb of 2:15, where the man was set in the park to guard it. The lexicon prints two entries under ὁδός; the first is the Attic word for *a threshold*, and the way is the second.

reading: and [[threw|threw, cast out of, threw out, cast out and banished, deposed, threw away and rejected|ἐκβάλλω]] the [[name:Αδαμ]] and [[removed to|removed to, planted, settled, established as a colonist, restored to one's country|κατοικίζω]] him [[opposite|opposite, against|ἀπέναντι]] [[of the park|of the park, of the garden of Eden, of paradise|παράδεισος]] [[of the softness|of the softness, of the delicacy and daintiness, of the luxuries, of the luxuriousness and wantonness|τρυφή]] and [[arranged|arranged, put in order, drew up in order of battle, posted and stationed, appointed|τάσσω]] the [[name:χερουβιμ]] and [[the flaming|the flaming, the fiery, the flame-coloured|φλόγινος]] [[large sword|large sword, scymitar|ῥομφαία]] [[the one turning itself|the one turning itself, turning round, turning about, turning to and fro, turning back, revolving|στρέφω]] [[to keep watch and ward|to keep watch and ward, to keep guard, to watch and guard and keep and defend|φυλάσσω]] [[the way|the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method|ὁδός]] [[of the wood|of the wood, of the timber, of the piece of wood|ξύλον]] [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]].
